scout.name: Lighthouse Search Sprint
scout.notes: Remote hackathon open to adults worldwide. Free entry, solo participation allowed, and no face or voice requirements for submission.

reasons: The candidate meets all eligibility criteria: it is open to non-students, fully online, free to enter, offers a cash prize exceeding 100 USD, allows solo participation, has a future deadline, and does not require face or voice recording.

risks.risk: The organizer is not specified, which increases the risk of prize non-payment or lack of accountability for a remote-only event.

builder.idea: A privacy-focused, local-first semantic search engine for personal knowledge bases that uses a lightweight vector database to index local documents without cloud dependencies.
reuse: Vector embedding pipeline using open-source HuggingFace models
React-based UI boilerplate for search interfaces
Existing CI/CD scripts for automated documentation generation
steps: Initialize project with a local-first architecture to ensure no external API costs.
Implement document ingestion module for common formats (PDF, Markdown, TXT).
Integrate a local embedding model (e.g., all-MiniLM-L6-v2) to generate vector representations.
Build the search interface with real-time filtering and relevance ranking.
Package the solution as a portable CLI tool or desktop app to demonstrate 'Lighthouse' search capabilities.
Conduct stress testing on local document sets to ensure performance under 200ms latency.
demo_risks: Performance degradation on large document sets without proper indexing optimization.
Potential lack of organizer transparency regarding prize distribution (mitigated by focusing on high-quality code submission).
Dependency conflicts with local environment setups.

scout.name: Archive Lens Jam
scout.notes: The event is remote, free to enter, allows solo participation, and does not require face or voice recording. The deadline is in the future.

builder.idea: A lightweight browser-based tool that uses local browser APIs (File System Access API) to index and search through local archive folders (ZIP/TAR) without uploading data to a server, ensuring privacy and speed.
reuse: Local-first file indexing logic from previous search-based projects
UI component library for file tree visualization
Web Worker implementation for non-blocking archive extraction
steps: Implement a file picker interface using the File System Access API.
Develop a Web Worker to stream and index archive contents (metadata/filenames) without full extraction.
Build a fuzzy search engine using a lightweight library like FlexSearch.
Create a responsive dashboard to display search results and provide 'quick-look' previews.
Package as a static PWA for offline-first usage.
demo_risks: Browser memory limits when indexing very large archives.
Performance bottlenecks with deep directory nesting.
Lack of organizer transparency regarding prize payout (mitigated by keeping development time low).

reuse: Modular data ingestion pipeline from previous IoT projects

Build a React dashboard to visualize incoming data streams in real-time.

builder.idea: A graph-based knowledge visualization tool that uses LLM-extracted entities and relationships from user-uploaded documents to build an interactive, searchable 'atlas' of information.
reuse: Vector database integration logic from previous RAG projects
FastAPI boilerplate for document processing pipelines
steps: Set up a FastAPI backend to handle PDF/text ingestion and entity extraction using a free-tier LLM API.
Implement a graph database schema (using NetworkX or Neo4j) to store extracted entities and relationships.
Develop a frontend dashboard using D3.js or React-Force-Graph to visualize the knowledge atlas.
Add a semantic search feature to allow users to query the atlas and highlight relevant sub-graphs.
Package the solution as a containerized app with a clear README for the judges.
demo_risks: The organizer's legitimacy is unverified, risking time investment for a non-existent prize.
Potential latency issues with free-tier LLM APIs during entity extraction.
Complexity of visualizing large graphs in a browser without performance degradation.
